title: Amid a tumultuous season, Jarren Duran is starting to take off at perfect time for Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran has improved, batting .341 with an .856 OPS in his last 12 games amidst Boston's successful run.
Duran's recent performance included going 2-for-3 with a double and stolen base in a 4-0 win over the White Sox.
Despite earlier struggles, Duran's speed and hitting potential are crucial to the Red Sox's ongoing playoff pursuit.

title: Suspect arrested in fatal shooting of Dorchester man
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Hensly Dominique Jeanty, 32, arrested for the mid-July murder of Breidy Martinez in Dorchester, Boston Police announced.
Jeanty faces charges including murder and multiple firearm offenses, following an arrest warrant from Dorchester District Court.
Breidy Martinez, 29, was found dead from a gunshot on July 15 near 15 York St., Dorchester; investigation ongoing.

title: Worked killed after being pinned by tractor trailer at Mass. warehouse
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A 56-year-old man was killed at Chatham Village Foods warehouse in Wareham, Massachusetts, on Wednesday morning.
The victim was pinned by a tractor trailer behind a loading dock and was pronounced dead at 9:54 a.m.
The Plymouth County District Attorney's office is investigating the incident, and the victim's name has not been released.

title: Abreu homers again, Gray gets 14th victory as Red Sox beat White Sox 4-0 for 7th straight win
author: The Associated Press
bullets: The Boston Red Sox secured their seventh consecutive win, defeating the Chicago White Sox 4-0.
Sonny Gray achieved his 14th victory of the season, striking out eight in six innings.
Wilyer Abreu hit his 20th home run, marking his fourth in three games.

title: Huge basking shark spotted off South Shore beach, white sharks appear near Maine, Cape Cod
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A massive basking shark was spotted near Humarock Beach, Scituate, on August 4, drawing attention from beachgoers.
White sharks were seen near North Beach Island in Chatham and off Scarborough, Maine, prompting local warnings.
Sightings of sharks in New England are increasing due to peak season and advances in documentation technology.

title: Man shot to death mid-morning on Blue Hill Avenue
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was fatally shot near 564 Blue Hill Ave in Dorchester, Boston, on Wednesday morning.
The victim sought help and collapsed after being shot multiple times; he later died at a local hospital.
Boston Police are investigating and urge anyone with information to contact their Homicide Unit.

title: Former MLB GM says Red Sox had ‘biggest overpay’ before trade deadline
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Former MLB GM Jim Bowden labeled the Red Sox trade of Connelly Early for Curtis Mead as the biggest overpay.
Curtis Mead, acquired by the Red Sox, suffered a fractured wrist, sidelining him for six to eight weeks.
Connelly Early was traded despite an impressive 7-5 record and a 3.44 ERA in 17 starts for the Red Sox.

title: Brockton mayor suing state, says 2025 crash involving State Trooper left him disabled
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Brockton Mayor Moises Rodrigues is suing Massachusetts for negligence after a 2025 crash with a State Trooper.
Rodrigues claims the crash caused severe injuries, leading to $32,000 in medical bills and partial disability.
The lawsuit was filed after Trooper Augustine Moore declined an out-of-court settlement, with Rodrigues seeking a jury trial.

title: Grant Williams explains relationship dynamic between Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Grant Williams addressed the dynamic between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown, stating they respected and enjoyed working together.
The Celtics' duo was professionally successful, winning an NBA championship in 2024 despite not being close off the court.
Jayson Tatum expressed love and respect for Brown, refuting claims of animosity and highlighting nine successful seasons together.

title: Cyclospora cases climb to 147 in Mass., but officials say season remains within historical range
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Massachusetts reported 147 cyclospora cases from May to August 1, linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms.
Cyclospora symptom onset and diagnosis lag but numbers remain within historical ranges; no large outbreaks found in Massachusetts.
FDA links recalled iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico to cases; Massachusetts cases aren't linked to international travel.
